title: The assignment detail reads its own case; the tab stops loading every posting
acceptance: listCasePostings(caseA, wsA) where caseA has 2 postings, caseB has 3, and a corrupt caseA posting sits in wsB -> exactly caseA's 2 postings, each carrying `status` ('open'|'closed'); the SQL filters workspace_id and case_id, never a client-side filter

body:
## Summary
The assignment detail reader fetches its own case's channels, shortlist inputs and in-flight counts by id; the lifecycle list carries its per-case counts; and the Dev studio stops loading every posting, every submission and every evaluation in the workspace on mount and after each evaluation.

## Description
r03 split the case record off the list (GET /api/devcase/[id]) but left the other half of the same reader on `GET /api/devcase/postings`: a workspace-wide fold that inlines every submission of every posting (an N+1 with an unbounded per-posting read), joins outcomes and computes a promote verdict for each, and is re-fetched after every `evaluate_submission` and every lifecycle step. Its two consumers need far less: CaseDetail filters it down to one case client-side, and LifecycleSection folds it down to two integers per case. The move: (1) extract the enrichment (outcome join, promote preview, in-flight aggregate) from the postings route into `app/_lib/devcase-postings-view.ts` so both routes answer it identically; (2) a slice `app/_lib/db/devcase-case-postings.ts` with `listCasePostings(caseId, ws)` (SQL-scoped, status carried) and `caseIntakeCounts(caseIds, ws)` (one GROUP BY for submissions; in-flight folded from inFlightAttemptsByPosting); (3) `GET /api/devcase/[id]/channels` (requireOperator + the same owner check as [id]); (4) GET /api/devcase/lifecycle attaches `submissionCount` and `inFlight` per row; (5) CaseDetailById loads case + channels together under one version key that DevTab bumps on `evaluate_submission` and lifecycle completions; LifecycleSection reads counts off the row. The workspace route is kept, unchanged, for the e2e journeys.

Not a new slice of devcase.ts: that module is on every studio route's import graph (the devcase-ledger.ts precedent). No new table, no tenancy manifest change. Read-only - no read->write, so no lock strategy is needed. Perf: the channels route pulls the same graph the postings route does today (dev-outcomes, devcase-promote-verdict, devcase-orchestrator for activePromoteFloor) under the `app/api/**/route.ts` glob budget; the lifecycle route gains only the count slice + devcase-inflight, not the view module. Neither app/page.tsx nor the task-hub graph is touched. Must not share a wave with this context's slot-B card (both edit DevCaseDetail.tsx and DevTypes.ts).

## Flow
Open a row -> CaseDetailById fetches /api/devcase/{id} and /api/devcase/{id}/channels in parallel -> CaseDetail renders shortlist/cohort/channels from its own postings -> an evaluation finishes -> DevTab bumps the detail version (re-reads ONE case) and reloads lifecycles (counts ride the rows) -> no workspace fold is ever requested by the studio.

## Expected impact
Studio mount and every evaluation completion stop shipping the workspace's entire submission/evaluation corpus; the detail's data is scoped by SQL instead of by a client filter; the lifecycle section's counts cover exactly its rows. It also puts posting `status` on the detail's typed wire, which the client type drops today - the prerequisite for any honest live/closed rendering.

## Evaluation
Claim: the detail and lifecycle section read case-scoped data and the studio never loads the workspace posting fold.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass.
After: 6 of 6.
Method: gate - node:test over the view module, the new route (real handlers, temp KP_DB_PATH) and the lifecycle GET, plus the source guard; npm run test:perf for the route-graph budget; existing postings route.test.ts unchanged.
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture.

title: Closed intake reads closed: stop, reopen, and no dead links handed out
acceptance: intakeOf([]) -> {state:'unpublished'}; intakeOf([{status:'open'},{status:'closed'}]) -> {state:'live', open:1, closed:1}; intakeOf([{status:'closed'}]) -> {state:'closed', open:0, closed:1}

intakeAction({state:'live'}, lifecycleStage:null) -> 'stop'; ({state:'live'}, 'collecting') -> null (the lifecycle row's Close owns it); ({state:'closed'}, null|'closed') -> 'reopen'; ({state:'unpublished'}) -> 'publish'

POST /api/devcase/[id]/intake {action:'stop'} on a case with no lifecycle and one open posting (recruiter seat) -> 200 {closed:1}; the posting's status is 'closed'; POST /api/devcase/inbound with its token -> 410 POSTING_CLOSED; one dev_audit row action 'intake_stopped' ref=caseId
Same call on a case whose newest lifecycle is 'collecting' -> 409 DEVCASE_INTAKE_LIFECYCLE_OWNS and the posting is still 'open'
Repeat stop on the already-stopped case -> 200 {closed:0} (the UPDATE re-asserts status='open'; nothing re-written, no second audit row)
Viewer seat: POST /api/devcase/publish and POST /api/devcase/[id]/intake -> 403 coded; route-capability-coverage.test.ts ALLOWED no longer lists devcase/publish/route.ts

Ledger: a case with no lifecycle whose only posting is closed -> stage 'closed' (not 'published'), so devcase-sla's stall rule no longer flags it; an open posting still -> 'published'; facets include 'closed'
After a stop, POST /api/devcase/publish on the same case -> alreadyPublished:false and a token different from the stopped one (reopen mints a fresh link; the old one stays 410)
premise: app/features/tools/devcases/DevCaseDetail.tsx:66 `const published = casePostings.length > 0;` - any posting, open or closed, reads as live

app/features/tools/devcases/DevTypes.ts:157-170 - the client Posting type has no `status`, though the server row carries it (app/_lib/db/devcase.ts:668 in rowToPosting, used by listPostings at :754) and it is already on the wire
app/features/tools/devcases/DevCaseDetailHeader.tsx:109 disables Publish when `published` and :114 labels it 'Published' - a closed case can never be reopened from the UI
app/api/devcase/publish/route.ts:37-39 - the server deliberately treats a publish after a close-out as a genuine new posting; the UI simply cannot reach it

app/features/tools/devcases/DevCaseDetailChannels.tsx:37 renders the copy-link pill and :39 the manual-intake SubmissionForm for EVERY posting - a closed channel hands out a link that answers 410 (app/api/devcase/inbound/route.ts:67-72) and offers a form that the submit route refuses as POSTING_CLOSED (app/api/devcase/submit/route.ts:75)
app/features/tools/devcases/DevCaseDetail.tsx:189-193 - a closed case with no submissions shows the 'waiting for applicants' panel

app/features/tools/devcases/DevCaseDetail.tsx:94-97 - a per-posting close was explicitly deferred for lack of a door; the only close is the lifecycle's, so a case published from this detail (no lifecycle) has no way to stop intake at all

app/api/devcase/lifecycle/[id]/close/route.ts:41 - a second close of a closed lifecycle returns alreadyClosed BEFORE enumerating postings (:53), so a posting reopened after close-out could never be closed by that door - the stop door must exist before reopen is offered

app/_lib/db/devcase-ledger.ts:145 and :178 read 'published' whenever ANY posting exists; app/_lib/db/devcase-ledger.test.ts:65 names the rule 'an open posting reads published' but the SQL never checks status; app/_lib/devcase-sla.ts:17 counts 'published' as a stall-able open stage

app/api/route-capability-coverage.test.ts:115 - devcase/publish/route.ts is still an unjudged slice-2 door: minting a live candidate-facing token asks no capability, while its sibling POST /api/devcase asks pipeline:write (app/api/devcase/route.ts:96)
rollback: Revert the series: the stop door only flips dev_postings.status open->closed (the same write the lifecycle close makes) and a reopen is an ordinary publish, so no row is left in a state the pre-change code cannot read; the ledger SQL change is a projection only; the capability gate reverts by restoring the ALLOWED line.
runner_up: Publish flow as one tested reducer: confirming/ack/publishing/published collapse from 19 threaded props (DevCaseDetailHeader.tsx:13-53) into a pure state machine - dropped as mostly a refactor once the intake state above exists.
body:
## Summary
The assignment detail tells live intake from closed intake and lets the recruiter act on it: a live case with no lifecycle can be stopped, a closed case can be reopened (a fresh link, the old one stays dead), closed channels stop offering their dead link and a manual-intake form that is refused, and the Assignments table stops calling a closed case 'published'.

## Description
The store has had open/closed postings since W5-3 and the publish route already reopens after a close, but the detail never reads the status: `published = casePostings.length > 0`. So after a close-out (or the r07 fence withdrawing a token) the header says Published and is disabled, every channel card still copies an apply URL that answers 410 and offers a form the submit route refuses, and a closed case with no applicants says it is waiting for them. A case published from this detail (no lifecycle) has no way to stop intake at all - the detail's own comment records the deferral. The ledger repeats the confusion in SQL, which also lets the stall chip fire on a closed case.

Build: (1) `devcaseIntakeState.ts` - `intakeOf(postings)` -> unpublished | live | closed with counts, and `intakeAction(intake, lifecycleStage)` -> publish | stop | reopen | null; (2) `POST /api/devcase/[id]/intake {action:'stop'}` - requireOperator, `requireCapabilityCoded('pipeline:write')`, ownedDevCase, then `closeCaseIntake(caseId, ws)` in devcase.ts: a `db.transaction(...).immediate()` that reads the case's newest lifecycle and refuses (409 DEVCASE_INTAKE_LIFECYCLE_OWNS) unless it is absent or 'closed', then `UPDATE dev_postings SET status='closed' WHERE workspace_id=? AND case_id=? AND status='open'` (lock AND re-check: the write lock keeps an orchestrator mint from interleaving, the WHERE makes a repeat a zero-change no-op). It sends NO candidate comms - stopping intake is not a rejection; the lifecycle's Close stays the door that wraps up submitters (closing-withdraws-candidates-in-flight). recordAudit({actor:'human', action:'intake_stopped', ref: caseId}); (3) publish asks `pipeline:write` (the reopen half must not be looser than the stop half); (4) UI - every surface that shows the status or offers the refused action: header button (Publish / Stop intake / Reopen, disabled with a reason when a live lifecycle owns intake), DevPublishConfirm gains a reopen variant saying the old link stays closed, channel cards render closed channels with a closed chip, the token as inert text and no SubmissionForm, the waiting panel says intake is closed; (5) ledger stage: open posting -> 'published', only closed postings -> 'closed'. New codes DEVCASE_INTAKE_LIFECYCLE_OWNS (REFUSAL) and DEVCASE_INTAKE_STOP_FAILED (STORE) = four catalog entries each, plus the UI keys, in all four locales. The route is NOT admitted by app/_lib/auth/public-routes.ts (it only lists /api/devcase/session and /api/devcase/inbound), so it sits behind the fail-closed gate; api-reference.md regenerated with npm run api:docs. No new table. Stop's fetch lives in CaseDetail (the LifecycleRow close precedent), so DevTab/useDevTabActions are untouched. Must not share a wave with slot A (DevCaseDetail.tsx, DevTypes.ts).

## Flow
Open a manual live assignment -> header shows 'Live - Stop intake' -> confirm -> postings close, cards show Closed, apply link now inert, ledger row reads Closed -> later 'Reopen' -> confirm names that a new link is minted and the old one stays closed -> publish mints a fresh open posting -> 'Stop intake' is available again. On a lifecycle-run assignment that is still collecting, the header states that the lifecycle row's Close ends intake (with wrap-up notes).

## Expected impact
A recruiter can finally end intake on an assignment published by hand, can reopen one that was closed, never copies a dead link to a candidate, never types a manual submission into a refused form, and the Assignments table's stage and stall chip stop contradicting the store. Also closes one slice-2 capability door.

## Evaluation
Claim: intake state is read from posting status on every surface that shows it, and stop/reopen are offered exactly when they are legal.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test over devcaseIntakeState.ts, the intake and publish routes driven as real handlers with seat fixtures (write-capability-gate precedent), devcase-ledger.test.ts; npm run i18n:check, api:check, test:unit.
Result: pending build.
Gate: policy-tighten.
